warnings.title: Negative-control bounds appear fitted to observed rank rather than independently derived
warnings.detail: For 20 of 24 questions the declared max_rank equals exactly the negative target's observed rank minus one. The rule implied by several reason strings, that the negative must not outrank the expected source, explains only 3 of 24 and is contradicted by LR-Q011 (bound 2, expected targets at 1 and 10), LR-Q003 (bound 4, expected at 1 and 9) and LR-Q017 (bound 2, expected at 1, 2 and 4). The controls therefore pass by construction on this bundle, though they are live against regression: a single rank position trips 20 of them. Three negatives (LR-Q008, LR-Q016, LR-Q021) do not rank at all for their queries so cannot fire, and LR-Q015's ranks 24 against a bound of 10. The choice of negative target is in every case a genuine, well-reasoned near miss; the weakness is in the derivation of the bound, not the selection of the target. This is a substantial improvement on the prior inert control and does not block acceptance.

warnings.title: Two thirds of required caveat assertions use universally declared caveat IDs
warnings.detail: CAV-BOUNDED-COVERAGE, CAV-DATE-SEPARATION, CAV-RIGHTS-AND-ACCESS and CAV-SOURCE-AUTHORITY are declared on all 2,203 records; only CAV-NO-RESTRICTED-AUTOMATION (212), CAV-BOUNDARY-NOT-CONCLUSION (22), CAV-ACCESSIBLE-JOURNEY (11) and CAV-LANGUAGE-DISTINCTION (10) discriminate. Across the suite 32 of 48 required caveat assertions name a universal ID, and 10 of 24 questions (LR-Q001, Q003, Q008, Q009, Q010, Q011, Q013, Q018, Q021, Q022) have entirely universal requirements, so for those the runtime caveat assertion would pass on any record the Explorer opened. This does not block acceptance because each journey independently asserts the expected canonical source URL as an anchor href and clicks the specific expected record, pinning selection by evidence that does not depend on caveat discrimination, and because the four universal propositions genuinely do apply to every record. The precise claim the runtime evidence supports is that the Explorer renders the governed caveat controls for the selected record; it establishes a question-specific requirement only for the 16 selective assertions.

warnings.title: A caveat can satisfy its assertion as a bare identifier
warnings.detail: 2,196 of 2,203 records declare more caveat IDs than prose caveats, and the rendered context_note appends a 'Caveat controls: <IDs>' trailer. Where a declared ID has no matching prose sentence the user sees an opaque token, and the runtime assertion is satisfied by that token. Substantive communication is good overall and the prose caveats inspected for all 24 questions are strong, but rendering the caveat-registry text for every declared ID would close the gap between what is asserted and what is communicated.

warnings.title: Retrieval evidence characterises the diagnostic baseline, not the shipped worker
warnings.detail: data/search/index.json is absent, so both the shipped diagnostic and this reviewer's harness scored data/catalogue.json with on-the-fly tokenisation while the Explorer consumes data/explorer/search/ shards. This is now correctly handled: the diagnostic is explicitly non-formal, record_source self-reports catalogue-fallback, and formal source and caveat evidence comes from the locked-Explorer receipt instead. The residual consequence is that the ranks in EW-001 and the metrics above describe the baseline, not the ordering a user of the pinned Explorer sees.

warnings.title: Recall and result-ordering observations from the held-out pass
warnings.detail: Precision was acceptable in all eight cases: every returned record was relevant to its query and correctly caveated, and no irrelevant or unsafe record was surfaced anywhere in the pass. Three cases nonetheless showed weak recall or suboptimal ordering. RV-002 returned a single record for a third-party-rights query, omitting the OCOD and Price Paid Data records that carry the clearest Ordnance Survey and Royal Mail conditions. RV-006 returned one record for a Welsh forms and correspondence query and did not surface the bundle's only Welsh-language glossary record. RV-008 ranked adverse-possession guidance first for an unregistered-land query while the directly responsive corrective, 'Some land is unregistered, some interests are not registrable and pending applications may not yet appear', sat at rank 4. These are lexical-overlap artifacts of the diagnostic baseline described in EW-004 and no hard failure followed from any of them. This reviewer initially characterised these as precision failures and corrected that: the deficiency is in recall and ordering, not in the relevance of what was returned.

limitations: This is an AI-agent evaluation review. It is not independent human HM Land Registry assurance, not human domain expertise in land registration, not legal advice, not a licence or intellectual-property audit, not a privacy or data-protection assessment, not a security assessment, not an accessibility audit or conformance assertion, and not participant or user research. RISK-015 remains a residual risk this review does not discharge.

No live official source was fetched and no publisher page was re-observed. Expected propositions were verified against the frozen candidate and its recorded source evidence; the suite correctly frames them as bounded acceptance expectations rather than gold answers and this review does not upgrade them. Source drift since the 2026-07-29 cutoff is unmeasured.

No restricted service was contacted, no account created, no payment made, no authenticated API called, and no credential, certificate, session or signed link handled. The Business Gateway closure was verified from published record metadata only.

The locked-Explorer runtime receipts were read, digest-checked and cross-verified against the journey definitions, but this reviewer did not re-execute the browser journeys and has no independent observation of the rendered DOM. Conclusions about visible caveat assertion rest on the journey definitions, the passed digest-bound receipt and the projected context_note content in the Explorer data plane.

Accessibility dimensions were assessed from declared statements, record metadata and static markup. No keyboard, screen-reader, focus, zoom or contrast testing was performed, so HF-ACCESSIBILITY was reviewed as a metadata and display-obligation question rather than an executed accessibility test.
Welsh-language dimensions were assessed from source-native labels and normalised language metadata. Translation quality was not evaluated and no bilingual-parity conclusion is offered.
This reviewer is not the project owner. No Land Registry G9 approval was created, no deployment variable set, no publication authorised, and no public or Pages URL visited or verified.
